string.name: knowledge_k1_title
string.value: What are carbon peaking and carbon neutrality

string.name: knowledge_k1_summary
string.value: Emissions peak then decline; neutrality is when emissions equal absorption.

string.name: knowledge_k1_content
string.value: Carbon peaking means CO2 emissions reach their historical maximum, plateau, then decline sustainably. Carbon neutrality means offsetting one's emissions within a period through tree planting, energy saving and emission reduction, achieving “net zero”. This is China's solemn commitment to the world and a broad, profound systemic socioeconomic transformation.

string.name: knowledge_k1_p1
string.value: Peaking: emissions stop growing after the peak

string.name: knowledge_k1_p2
string.value: Neutrality: emissions offset by absorption, net zero

string.name: knowledge_k1_p3
string.value: National goals: peak before 2030, neutral before 2060

string.name: knowledge_k1_p4
string.value: Key paths: energy transition, efficiency, ecological carbon sinks

string.name: knowledge_k2_title
string.value: Comparing carbon footprints of daily travel

string.name: knowledge_k2_summary
string.value: Walking and cycling are near zero; buses and subways next; private cars highest.

string.name: knowledge_k2_content
string.value: Carbon emissions per kilometre differ notably by mode. Walking and cycling emit almost nothing; buses and subways are lower thanks to per-capita sharing; private petrol cars emit the most. Choose walking or cycling for short trips and public transport for longer ones — the most direct and sustainable way to cut emissions.

string.name: knowledge_k2_p1
string.value: Walk / cycle: near-zero emissions and good exercise

string.name: knowledge_k2_p2
string.value: Bus / subway: low per-capita emissions, good for longer trips

string.name: knowledge_k2_p3
string.value: Private petrol car: highest emissions per kilometre

string.name: knowledge_k2_p4
string.value: Rule: walk or cycle short trips, take public transport for longer ones

string.name: knowledge_k3_summary
string.value: Air conditioning, lighting and standby power are the main sources of home electricity use.

string.name: knowledge_k3_content
string.value: Household electricity is a major source of residential emissions. AC temperature, lighting and standby appliances all hide room for savings. Habits like turning off lights, unplugging idle devices and washing in batches add up to significant reductions over time — and lower your bills directly.

string.name: knowledge_k3_p1
string.value: Keep summer AC at 26°C or higher; each 1°C higher saves more

string.name: knowledge_k3_p3
string.value: Unplug standby devices to cut “phantom” power use

string.name: knowledge_k3_p4
string.value: Keep the fridge away from heat and defrost regularly; wash in batches

string.name: knowledge_k4_title
string.value: The value of sorting and recycling

string.name: knowledge_k4_summary
string.value: Recycling gives materials a second life and markedly cuts virgin-production emissions.

string.name: knowledge_k4_content
string.value: Reusing recovered resources such as waste paper, plastic, metal, glass and old clothes can greatly cut the energy and emissions of producing virgin materials. Rinsing and sorting before disposal improves recycled quality. Old clothes have the highest reduction factor — never just throw them away.

string.name: knowledge_k4_p1
string.value: Paper, plastic, metal, glass and old clothes are all recyclable

string.name: knowledge_k4_p2
string.value: Recycling cuts energy and emissions from virgin production

string.name: knowledge_k4_p3
string.value: Rinse and sort before disposal to improve recycled quality

string.name: knowledge_k4_p4
string.value: Old clothes have the highest factor — don't toss them

string.name: knowledge_k5_summary
string.value: Reducing food waste and eating more plant-based meals both cut emissions.

string.name: knowledge_k5_content
string.value: Food carries carbon emissions from production, transport and cooking, so wasting food wastes that carbon. Finishing your plate, ordering only what you need, cutting disposable tableware and adding more plant-based meals are simple, effective and healthy low-carbon choices.

string.name: knowledge_k5_p1
string.value: Food carries emissions across its whole life cycle

string.name: knowledge_k5_p2
string.value: Clean plate = less waste = fewer emissions

string.name: knowledge_k5_p3
string.value: Eat more plant-based meals — good for emissions and health

string.name: knowledge_k5_p4
string.value: Bring your own tableware to cut disposables

string.name: knowledge_k6_title
string.value: How to calculate a personal carbon footprint

string.name: knowledge_k6_content
string.value: A personal carbon footprint is usually estimated as “activity data × emission factor”. Emission factors come from authoritative measurement and statistics, reflecting the emission intensity per unit of activity. This app ships a factor library for common low-carbon actions — just enter the amount to estimate your savings automatically.

string.name: knowledge_k6_p2
string.value: Factors come from authoritative measurement and statistics

string.name: knowledge_k6_p3
string.value: The app ships a factor library for common actions

string.name: knowledge_k6_p4
string.value: Enter an amount to estimate savings automatically
